propositions: The _paged_search pager in _base.py:141-157 has no offset-stall guard; when a server ignores/repeats startAt offsets, the loop never exits because the only break condition is an empty batch, causing unbounded growth of the output.
A startAt-ignoring server measured spinning 26 calls requesting [0,3,6,9,...] offsets while receiving the same page 1 every time, terminating only by harness cap rather than pager logic.

The fail-open exception handler in get_parent_map (_hierarchy.py:91) wraps _paged_search in a bare except Exception clause that converts any pager-level abort into a silent empty parent map, neutralizing the loud signal.

The three whole-project readers (get_issuelinks_map, get_comment_map, get_parent_map) feed into fetcher.fetch_snapshot behind broad fail-open handlers at lines 610, 652, 688 that would swallow a stall error raised at the transport boundary.

The defect class is proven by parity gaps: fetcher._iter_pages guards offset stall (raising SilentTruncationError), acli_graph raises RunawayPaginationError for cursor stall, but _paged_search lacks any stall guard despite serving the same offset-paged whole-project search operation.

A fix must add a dedicated BackendPaginationStallError in core (so fetcher can name it without importing adapters), track the previous page's first key in _paged_search, raise on ANY repeated page (short or full, per DC's forced small-page design), and re-raise past all four fail-open sites.
